newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK & Shanghai Hotels reviews Sydney plans.
newsitem.headline: HK & Shanghai Hotels reviews Sydney plans.

text.p: Hongkong and Shanghai Hotels Ltd said on Monday it was reviewing various development options for its site next to Sydney's famed opera house following weekend protests in Australia against the project.
"At the moment we are gathering all the data required to make an informed decision as to how we go forward," spokeswoman Kate Kelly said.

"We have three options, which are developing an economically viable hotel and apartment scheme which will fit within the approved planning guideline, or pursuing the pre-development application that we made last September for a hotel and apartment development, including our request for a minimal height increase to allow us to create a hotel to our standard," Kelly said.

"Or, if neither of the above options is viable, then abandoning, with great regret, proposals for the hotel and going ahead with the apartment block for which approval has already been granted," she said.

The hotel and apartment complex on the East Circular Quay has prompted opposition from some residents, including several thousand demonstrators over the weekend, who say it blocks the view of the Sydney Opera House, one of Australia's top tourist draws.
In June last year, Hongkong and Shanghai Hotels announced it had formed a partnership with Colonial Investment Management Plc to develop a 220-room Peninsula Hotel at the quay.

The company in fact had bought a 95 percent stake in the development of apartments on the site for A$200 million and said in its interim report published last July it would seek to include a Peninsula hotel on the site.
Colonial's original plans were for a four-block apartment complex. The Hong Kong company has proposed building two apartment blocks and converting the plans for the other two into a hotel.
The company further said it hoped to complete the hotel in time for the Olympic Games to be held in Sydney in 2000.
The development brought protests from residents for years before the hotel group entered the project, Kelly said.
Hongkong and Shanghai Hotels will announce its results for 1996 on Wednesday. Its shares closed HK$0.25 higher at HK$13.90 on Monday.
